observation: Manually developed, source-pinned bounded two-intervening-instruction compiler rewrite yielded 9 fewer decoded x86-64 guest instruction bytes and 3 fewer decoded guest instructions in three Rust-generated Wasm exports while keeping other live uses of intermediate product. Correctness evidence is finite Wasm executions/traps and separate arithmetic proofs of the pure unsigned relation, not a whole-compiler-pass proof.
native_cost_metric: count of decoded instruction encoding bytes in each named Wasmtime guest function, including trap paths; NOT whole-AOT or ELF .text bytes, NOT CLIF/ISLE costs, NOT dynamic throughput

source_and_machine_reachability.admitted_match: same-block i64 udiv(x,y); imul(q,y); iconst c; rotl(m,c); isub(x,m) with exact SSA edges, positive target x86-64, non-none optimization; retain imul for other uses
source_and_machine_reachability.unsupported: generic scheduler/nonadjacent operations, intervening calls/memory/traps, arbitrary register liveness, flags/poison/native state, signed division
source_and_machine_reachability.emitted_effect: 3 target exports eliminate a redundant native subtraction and adjust moves; imul remains live, hardware divq count unchanged
source_and_machine_reachability.controls: negative wrong_multiplier and out-of-vocabulary dual-chain exports show zero change in parsed native instruction-byte/instruction counts

whole_module.note: Whole-AOT and .text size are unchanged despite verified per-function native instruction savings; function layout/ELF padding prevents conflating metrics.

independent_recheck.status: passed, SHA and original native/AOT/CLIF cost receipt replay

separate_independent_symbol_audit.audited: five named guest symbols, same original archived Rust Wasm, disassembly, native cost, AOT/CLIF/ELF source and hash receipts, controls and finite test evidence

qualifications_and_nonclaims: This result is a manually designed Cranelift compiler-rewrite pilot, not a newly ZenoFCIS-synthesized sequence or a demonstration of general optimality.
Finite values and trap/panic agreement are not a proof of arbitrary SSA, debug-location, register allocator, trap location/ordering, flags, undefined/poison or machine-ISA state.
The bounded local same-block rule is not a review-ready upstream ISLE rule; no unconditionally applicable VeriISLE proof was obtained.
No reliable throughput/runtime improvement, general corpus prevalence, cross-target portability or whole-AOT size reduction is established.
The first 5 exports are deliberately constructed, not external representative production workloads.
Earlier 13-byte native-function savings from a distinct optimized Rust input remain separate and are not silently combined with these 9-byte results.
next_gate: Obtain comprehensive compiler-pass SSA/trap/register/target correctness, investigate how live uses behave across more code shapes, independently check exact emitted x86 under register pressure and align code-size savings with representative workload profitability. Only then consider a focused draft upstream PR.
